config.title: Renting a Boat in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: Licence-free motorboats, kayaks and SUP boards in Berlin: what you may rent, where the rules let you go, and what it costs.

items.q: Can I rent a boat in Berlin without a boat licence?
items.a: **Yes. Motorboats with up to 15 hp are licence-free in Germany**, and Berlin rental bases hand them out after a short briefing on site. Flotte Dahme at Strandbad Wendenschloss rents licence-free day boats for up to six people from about **180 EUR on a weekday**, with a fuel charge and a **250 EUR cash deposit** on top. Skippers usually need to be 18.

items.q: Can a rental boat drive past Museum Island and the Reichstag?
items.a: **No.** The Spree between the Kanzleramtssteg and the Oberbaumbruecke, including the Spreekanal around Museum Island, is closed to licence-free boats, kayaks and SUP boards all year. Only skippers with a German sport boat licence may enter, so the city-centre stretch belongs to commercial ships and sightseeing cruises. A one hour cruise from Friedrichstraße costs about **22.50 EUR**.

items.q: Where can I kayak or stand-up paddle in Berlin?
items.a: The classic runs are the **Landwehrkanal through Kreuzberg**, open to paddlers in both directions with a 6 km/h speed cap, and the **Spree east of the Oberbaumbruecke** around Rummelsburger Bucht and Treptower Park. Kanuliebe on the Insel der Jugend rents kayaks and SUP boards from about **15 EUR per hour**, and Ahoi Ostkreuz at Rummelsburger Bucht takes walk-ins. You may paddle up to the Oberbaumbruecke, then you have to turn.

items.q: How much does it cost to rent a boat in Berlin?
items.a: Rough 2026 season figures from the operators' own price lists: kayaks and SUP boards about **15 EUR per hour** in Treptower Park, day kayaks about **28 to 40 EUR** on the Havel side in Spandau, licence-free 15 hp day boats from about **180 EUR on a weekday** for up to six people, and the one hour sightseeing cruise about **22.50 EUR per person**. Most bases want cash for the deposit.

items.q: Can I swim in the Spree in central Berlin?
items.a: **No. Swimming is banned in the entire inner-city area**, both in the Spree and in the canals, under Berlin's bathing water rules. The allowed swimming water is outside the centre, at the lakes: the Mueggelsee in the southeast and the Wannsee lidos in the southwest are the classic choices.
